title: From 9/11 to Pahalgam: India’s Evolving Strategy in the Global War on Terror
gist: Framing 9/11 as an event that irreversibly altered a nation's trajectory, the article sets up India's own evolving counterterrorism posture — from the 20-year US campaign that killed bin Laden in Pakistan to India's post-Pahalgam Operation Sindoor — as the same kind of inflection.

insights.claim: Some incidents in world history not only leave deep scars on a nation's soul but alter that nation's trajectory irreversibly, and the September 11, 2001 attack is presented as the archetype of that category.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Agarwal
insights.so_what: A reusable lens for assessing whether a security event is a headline or a regime change in national policy — the test is irreversibility of trajectory.
insights.quote: Some incidents in world history not only leave deep scars on the soul of a nation but alter the nation’s trajectory irreversibly.

insights.claim: Nineteen al-Qaida terrorists hijacked four passenger planes on September 11, 2001, two of which crashed into the Twin Towers and one into the Pentagon, producing a death count of almost 3,000.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Agarwal
insights.so_what: The casualty and scale baseline against which subsequent mass-casualty attacks and national responses are measured.
insights.locator: A perfectly normal morning turned into a horrific nightmare

insights.claim: National outrage after 9/11 led the United States to launch its most extensive military mission since the Vietnam War, pursuing al-Qaida and Osama bin Laden into Afghanistan.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Agarwal
insights.so_what: Demonstrates the scale of policy response a single mass-casualty attack can trigger — the template for assessing potential reactions to future attacks.
insights.locator: The resultant national outrage and anger led to the United States

insights.claim: A military campaign lasting almost 20 years largely neutralized al-Qaida, and Osama bin Laden was eventually tracked and killed in Pakistan on May 2, 2011.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Agarwal
insights.so_what: That bin Laden was found in Pakistan rather than Afghanistan is the fact underpinning Indian arguments about cross-border sanctuary — the bridge to New Delhi's own counterterrorism case.
insights.locator: In a military campaign lasting almost 20 years

insights.claim: India conducted Operation Sindoor, after which Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited troops at Adampur Air Force Base in Punjab on May 13, 2025, marking a demonstrative shift in India's counterterrorism posture.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Agarwal
insights.so_what: India's move to overt kinetic retaliation raises the baseline escalation risk in any future India-Pakistan terrorism crisis.
insights.locator: Soldiers pose for a photo with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi

insights.claim: By placing the Pahalgam attack in the same analytical frame as 9/11, the argument is that India has crossed its own irreversible threshold in counterterrorism strategy rather than making an incremental adjustment.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Agarwal
insights.so_what: If India's doctrine has genuinely shifted rather than flexed, future attacks should be expected to produce military responses by default — a persistent South Asia risk premium.
